item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
318
ABNT20 KNHC 232344
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 PM EDT Wed Sep 23 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on newly formed
Tropical Depression Fay, located several hundred miles southwest of
the Azores.

Far Eastern Tropical Atlantic (AL90):
An area of low pressure located a few hundred miles southeast of the
Cabo Verde Islands is accompanied by a large area of disorganized
showers and thunderstorms. This system could become a short-lived
tropical depression on Thursday or Friday while it moves
northwestward to northward. However, strong upper-level winds
should end the opportunity for development by the weekend.
Interests in the Cabo Verde Islands should monitor the progress of
this system as gusty winds, areas of heavy rain and flash flooding
are possible there by Friday.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...60 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

&&

Public Advisories on Tropical Depression Fay are issued under WMO
header WTNT31 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPAT1.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Depression Fay are issued under WMO
header WTNT21 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMAT1.

$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Summary for Tropical Storm Fay (AT1/AL062026)
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...FAY REGAINS TROPICAL STORM STATUS... As of 3:00 AM GMT Thu Sep 24 the center of Fay was located near 29.8, -40.0 with movement WSW at 9 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1010 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 40 mph.

item.title: Tropical Storm Fay Public Advisory Number 16
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM GMT Thu Sep 24 2026 
921 
WTNT31 KNHC 240234
TCPAT1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Fay Advisory Number  16
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
300 AM GMT Thu Sep 24 2026
 
...FAY REGAINS TROPICAL STORM STATUS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 AM GMT...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...29.8N 40.0W
ABOUT 935 MI...1505 KM WSW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WSW OR 250 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1010 MB...29.83 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 AM GMT (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Fay was
located near latitude 29.8 North, longitude 40.0 West. Fay is moving
toward the west-southwest near 9 mph (15 km/h). A generally 
westward motion with some decrease in forward speed is expected 
over the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 40 mph (65 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Little change in strength is forecast during the 
next day or two, with gradual weakening expected thereafter.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 70 miles (110 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1010 mb (29.83 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 AM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Tropical Depression Fay Forecast Discussion Number 15
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM GMT Wed Sep 23 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 232035
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Depression Fay Discussion Number  15
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 PM GMT Wed Sep 23 2026
 
Convection has redeveloped around the center of Fay and has 
persisted during the day.  An earlier ASCAT pass indicated that the 
system still had a well-defined circulation. Therefore, Fay meets 
the criteria to be classified as a tropical cyclone again.  
The earlier ASCAT pass showed a maximum wind vector of around 
31 kt and the most recent TAFB Dvorak classification was at T1.5/25 
kt.  Based on the given data, Fay's intensity is estimated to be 30 
kt.
 
The cyclone is moving just a little south of due west, or around 
260/8 kt, as it moves to the south of a low- to mid-level ridge to 
the northwest. Fay is expected to continue on this general motion 
for the next several days. The current NHC track forecast is in 
line with the HCCA and GDMI forecast aids.
 
There is a brief opportunity for Fay to regain tropical storm 
status during the next day or so, however wind shear is expected to
increase again after 36 h. This should lead to the cyclone 
gradually weakening again, with the system becoming a post-tropical 
remnant low by 60 h, and then dissipating around 96 h, as 
suggested by simulated satellite imagery from the ECMWF global 
model.  The current NHC intensity forecast track is in line with 
both the HCCA and GDMI forecast aids.
